name: What is involved in widening interior doorways for wheelchair or walker access?

mainEntity.name: What is involved in widening interior doorways for wheelchair or walker access?

acceptedAnswer.text: Widening a doorway requires more than simply removing the existing trim; it often involves structural reframing, electrical adjustments, and drywall patching. Standard interior doors are usually 28 to 30 inches wide, whereas comfortable wheelchair clearance requires at least 32 to 36 inches of clear space. Because HH Remodeling specializes in framing, finish carpentry, and seamless drywall repair, the surrounding wall is opened, reframed, textured, and painted to match the adjacent living space cleanly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Widening a doorway involves cutting back drywall, reframing the rough opening, relocating any hidden electrical wiring, and installing a new jamb, trim, and drywall finish.
